Text:
What makes you happy? Not the big things — not the vacations or the milestones. The small, specific, ordinary things.

Mine: the particular silence of early morning. A book I can't put down. The smell of something baking when I didn't start it. Matcha made slowly. Letters that arrive by hand.

Tell me one of yours in the comments. I read every one.

"Forever is composed of nows."
— Emily Dickinson

This is a now. The kettle. The stillness. The first quiet hour before the day has opinions.

I don't optimize my mornings. I just try to be inside them.

Text:
I've been working on something for a long time. I want to tell you about it.

It's called Moss & Mail.

Every month, I write you a letter. By hand, on beautiful stationery, sealed with wax. I tuck in seeds for herbs or flowers. A recipe card. Art from a collaborating artist. A tea bag. A photo from the mountains near my home. A nature prompt. A Spotify playlist. A postcard with a stamp already on it — so you can send it to someone you love.

And a handwritten letter from me about what I'm reading, what I'm growing, what I'm struggling with, what I'm winning at.

It's a monthly letter subscription club. For people who still believe in the magic of opening a real envelope.
